family: CME Weather (the temperature-index complex: HDD / CDD / CAT monthly, seasonal-strip and quarterly-strip futures plus options on those futures). One schedule family, not a split.
products:
Listed on CME (XCME), Globex security group "HW" (options group "W7"), CME asset-class quadrant "Weather". Roots come from CME's own product-code sheet (https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/weather/files/weather-fact-card.pdf and https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/weather/files/updated-weather-product-slate.pdf):

US HDD monthly: H1 Atlanta, HW Boston, LP Burbank, H2 Chicago, H3 Cincinnati, HR Houston, H4 New York, H5 Dallas, H0 Las Vegas, HQ Minneapolis, HS Sacramento, H6 Philadelphia, H7 Portland. Seasonal strips append X (Nov-Mar) and Z (Dec-Feb): H1X/H1Z, HWX/HWZ, ... plus current Q1/Q4 quarterly strips.
US CDD monthly: K1, KW, KP, K2, K3, KR, K4, K5, K0, KQ, KS, K6, K7. Strips append K (May-Sep) and N (Jul-Aug), plus current Q2/Q3 quarterly strips.
European HDD monthly: D4 Essen, D0 London, D2 Amsterdam, D1 Paris (+X/Z strips).
European CAT monthly: G4 Essen, G0 London, G2 Amsterdam, G1 Paris (+K/N strips, + Q2/Q3 quarterly strips).
Pacific Rim CAT: G6 Tokyo (+G6X/G6Z/G6K/G6N strips).

Options carry the identical root as their future (CME Globex / CME ClearPort / Clearing codes are all e.g. H2 for Chicago HDD Monthly Options, K1N for Atlanta CDD Jul Seasonal Strip, G2N for Amsterdam CAT Jul Seasonal Strip). Summing futures + options across monthly, seasonal and quarterly strips gives the ~179-root figure. CME's weather landing page describes the complex as "index-based products geared to average seasonal and monthly weather in 18 cities globally" (13 US, 4 Europe, 1 Asia).

Historically the same key also covered now-delisted CME weather families that shared the identical grid: Canadian HDD/CDD/CAT, Australian HDD/CDD, Asia-Pacific monthly/seasonal, US Weekly Weather, Rainfall, Snowfall, Frost and the CME Hurricane Index products.
timezone:
America/Chicago (US/Central). CME publishes every weather window in Chicago time regardless of the underlying city — the Tokyo CAT and European CAT/HDD contracts carry the same CT grid as the US contracts.

Verbatim, CME weather contract-specs page (2010-2015 layout): "Trading Hours / (All times listed are Central Time) / CME Globex (Electronic Platform)" — https://web.archive.org/web/20100206082420id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading/weather/temperature/us-monthly-weather-heating_contract_specifications.html

Verbatim, CME weather trading-hours page: "Trading hours are in U.S. Central Time unless otherwise stated." — https://web.archive.org/web/20120503104742id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/weather-hours.html

Verbatim, live Tokyo CAT Monthly Futures specs (retrieved 2026-09-05): "CME Globex: Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. CT with a 60-minute break each day beginning at 4:00 p.m. CT" — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/cat/tokyo-cat-monthly/specs
current_grid:
All times America/Chicago, end-exclusive, seconds-since-midnight in brackets. REGULAR (RTH): NONE. Weather has no pit and no exchange-designated regular session today. CME's own Daily Bulletin Section 24 header states the RTH/ETH convention and Globex is the ETH side: "FOR PRODUCTS THAT ARE TRADED IN BOTH Open Outcry(RTH) AND on CME Globex (ETH) ... ETH REPRESENTS GLOBEX VOLUME TRANSACTIONS FROM THE GLOBEX(R) ELECTRONIC SESSION ONLY." — https://www.cmegroup.com/daily_bulletin/current/Section24_Weather_Futures_And_Options.pdf (Fri, Sep 04, 2026 issue). Every current weather product record carries pitEligible=0. This matches the repo's existing treatment of the analogous wrap-around CME/NYMEX/COMEX electronic families (energy_metals.rs uses regular: &[]). EXTENDED (executable CME Globex, wraps midnight): Sunday 17:00 [61200] -> Monday 16:00 [57600], and Monday-Thursday 17:00 [61200] -> next-day 16:00 [57600]. i.e. one rule set days = SUN + MON..THU, open_ssm 61200, close_ssm 57600. Friday's close is therefore 16:00 CT; there is a 60-minute halt 16:00-17:00 every trading day. Verbatim, live CME contract specs (retrieved 2026-09-05): "TRADING HOURS / CME Globex: / Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m. CT with a 60-minute break each day beginning at 4:00 p.m. CT" - Futures: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/hdd/chicago-hdd-monthly/specs - Options: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/hdd/chicago-hdd-monthly/specs/options - US CDD seasonal strip: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/cdd/atlanta-cdd-jul-seasonal-strip/specs - European CAT seasonal-strip options: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/cat/amsterdam-cat-jul-seasonal-strip/specs/options - Pacific Rim CAT: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/cat/tokyo-cat-monthly/specs (The legacy .contractSpecs.html / .contractSpecs.options.html URLs 301 to these /specs paths.) ORDER_ENTRY (CME Globex Pre-Open, nothing matches): Sunday 16:00 [57600] -> 17:00 [61200]; Monday-Thursday 16:45 [60300] -> 17:00 [61200]. Verbatim, SER-9519 table column "CME Globex Pre-Open Hours (unchanged)": "Sunday 4:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. CT / Monday – Thursday 4:45 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. CT" — https://www.cmegroup.com/content/dam/cmegroup/notices/ser/2025/03/ser-9519.pdf has_daily_close: true — "with a 60-minute break each day beginning at 4:00 p.m. CT" (live specs, URLs above); "daily trading halts 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. CT" (Globex Notice 2025-04-07). has_weekend_close: true — the week runs Sunday 17:00 to Friday 16:00 with no Friday-evening reopen; the next queue is Sunday 16:00. DO NOT MODEL AS A SESSION — CME ClearPort. The same specs pages publish "CME ClearPort: Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 5:45 p.m. CT with no reporting Monday - Thursday from 5:45 p.m. – 6:00 p.m. CT". ClearPort is submission-of-already-negotiated-trades for clearing, not a matching venue and not an order queue on the central limit order book, so it belongs in neither extended nor order_entry. SER-7606R (14 March 2016) is the primary document that put weather on ClearPort: "Effective Sunday, March 20, 2016 for trade date Monday, March 21, 2016 ... shall make the existing weather futures and options contracts provided in Table 1 below (the "Contracts") available for submission for clearing via CME ClearPort." — https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7606R.pdf GRID IN FORCE FROM THE JANUARY-2010 FLOOR UNTIL THE 2025 CUTOVER (the only other profile in scope): extended: Sunday 17:00 [61200] -> 15:15 [54900], Monday-Thursday 17:00 -> next-day 15:15; daily halt 15:15-17:00; regular: none. Verbatim, CME contract specs captured 2010-02-06 (nearest primary capture above the January-2010 floor): "Trading Hours / (All times listed are Central Time) / CME Globex (Electronic Platform) / SUN 5:00 p.m. - FRI 3:15 p.m. / Daily trading halts 3:15 p.m. - 5:00 p.m." — https://web.archive.org/web/20100206082420id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading/weather/temperature/us-monthly-weather-heating_contract_specifications.html The identical text was verified on CME captures of the same specification at 2010-07-25, 2012-05-11, 2013-09-10, 2015-09-04, 2016-12-01, 2018-06-01, 2019-11-18, 2021-04-22 (same URL, different Wayback timestamps: 20100725183017, 20120511155857, 20130910083357, 20150904012217, 20161201142405, 20180601223954, 20191118133125, 20210422172808) and, server-rendered inside the new product page, at 2021-07-28 and 2022-06-30 ("TRADING HOURS","specText":"

Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 3:15 p.m.
Daily trading halts 3:15 p.m. - 5:00 p.m.

") — https://web.archive.org/web/20220630073135id_/https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/temperature/us-monthly-weather-heating.contractSpecs.options.html Notably weather did NOT follow the 2015-09-21 NYMEX/COMEX close move to 16:00 CT: the 2015-09-04 and 2016-12-01 captures both still read 3:15 p.m. ONE FAMILY, NOT A SPLIT — evidence: (a) SER-9519 changes "all weather futures and options on weather contracts" in a single table, with one set of hours. (b) CME Globex Notice 2025-04-07: "The trading hours and daily trading halt for all weather products will be updated to ...". (c) At the 2010 floor the identical "SUN 5:00 p.m. - FRI 3:15 p.m. / Daily trading halts 3:15 p.m. - 5:00 p.m." text appears on the US HDD, European CAT, Asia-Pacific Seasonal, Canadian CAT, Rainfall and Hurricane specifications (Wayback ids 20100206082955, 20100206082842, 20100728121927, 20101125113353 on the corresponding /trading/weather/... pages; hurricane at 20100204205625 reads "Offered exclusively on the CME Globex electronic trading platform on Sundays through Thursdays, 5:00 p.m. – 3:15 p.m. CT the following day"). (d) CME's dedicated weather trading-hours page lists every US / Canadian / European / Asia-Pacific / Australian / weekly row with identical Pre-Open and electronic values — https://web.archive.org/web/20150406000146id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/weather-hours.html (e) Today, futures and options, monthly and seasonal strip, US / European / Pacific Rim all render the same Globex line (five live URLs above). (f) CME's Daily Bulletin puts every weather sub-group (WEATHER INDEX FUTURES, WEATHER STRIPS INDEX FUTURES, EUROPEAN WEATHER INDEX FUTURES, CAT EUROPEAN SEASONAL STRIP FUTURES, ADDITIONAL WEATHER FUTURES, and the matching options sections) in one section 24. So ONE key suffices for the whole complex; no US/European/seasonal split is needed.

revisions.change:
CME Globex executable window extended: daily close moved from 15:15 CT to 16:00 CT and the daily trading halt moved from 15:15-17:00 CT to 16:00-17:00 CT, for ALL weather futures and options on weather futures. The Sunday 17:00 CT open is unchanged; the CME Globex Pre-Open queues (Sunday 16:00-17:00 CT, Monday-Thursday 16:45-17:00 CT) are unchanged; CME ClearPort hours unchanged. New extended rule: days = SUN + MON..THU, open_ssm 61200, close_ssm 57600 (was 54900).

DATE KEYING — READ BEFORE ENCODING. CME states BOTH days and they mean different things. The SER landing page stamps "Effective Date: 14 April 2025" and the notice body says "Effective Sunday, April 13, 2025, for trade date Monday, April 14, 2025". The first session whose behaviour actually differs is the one that OPENS Sunday 2025-04-13 at 17:00 CT and now closes Monday 2025-04-14 at 16:00 CT instead of 15:15. Because this crate's wrapped rules are keyed by the LOCAL OPENING DAY, 2025-04-13 is the correct key here — exactly the precedent already recorded in energy_metals.rs ("The revision is keyed to Sunday 2015-09-20, the local opening day of that Monday trade-date session, so a wrapped rule gives Monday the sourced close."). An implementation that keys by trade date instead must use 2025-04-14. Both days are primary-sourced; neither is inferred.

("CME" or "Exchange") will expand the CME Globex electronic trading ("CME Globex") hours of all weather futures and options on weather contracts (the "Contracts") as detailed in the table below."  Table row "Weather Futures and Options on Weather Futures": CME ClearPort Hours (unchanged) = "Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 5:45 p.m. CT with no reporting Monday - Thursday from 5:45 p.m. – 6:00 p.m. CT"; CME Globex Pre-Open Hours (unchanged) = "Sunday 4:00 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. CT / Monday – Thursday 4:45 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. CT"; Current CME Globex Hours = "Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 3:15 p.m. / Daily trading halts 3:15 p.m. - 5:00 p.m."; Expanded CME Globex Hours = "Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 4:00 p.m. / Daily trading halts 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m."  Closing line: "Note that the CME Globex Pre-Open hours and the hours for trades submitted for clearing via CME ClearPort of the Contracts shall remain unchanged."

CORROBORATING PRIMARY #1 — the SER's own landing page (https://www.cmegroup.com/notices/ser/2025/03/ser-9519.html): "# SER-9519 / Notice Date: 10 March 2025 / Effective Date: 14 April 2025".

CORROBORATING PRIMARY #2 — CME Globex Notice, April 7, 2025 (https://www.cmegroup.com/notices/electronic-trading/2025/04/20250407.html), item "Trading Hours Change for Weather Products - This Week": "Effective this Sunday, April 13 (trade date Monday, April 14), The trading hours and daily trading halt for all weather products will be updated to Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 4:00 p.m. Central Time (CT) with daily trading halts 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. CT. The daily halt is communicated via the MDP Security Status (tag 35-Msg-Type=f) message where tag 326-SecurityTradingStatus=2 (Trading Halt)."  The same item is headlined "Trading Hours Change for Weather Products - April 13" in the Globex Notices of March 17, 2025 and March 24, 2025.

unsourced: ONSET OF THE PRE-OPEN (ORDER-ENTRY) QUEUES — NOT DATED. SER-9519 (2025-03-10) is the primary source for the current queues (Sunday 16:00-17:00 CT, Monday-Thursday 16:45-17:00 CT) and calls them "unchanged", but it gives no onset day, so the crate cannot date them. What the archive DOES show, on CME's own weather trading-hours page (https://web.archive.org/web/<ts>id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/weather-hours.html): the 2009-07-27 and 2011-09-27 layouts have NO Pre-Open columns at all (columns are Product Name | Open Outcry | Electronic Trading (Weekday) | Electronic Trading (Sunday) | CME ClearPort), so the January-2010 floor queue is simply unsourced. The 2012-05-03, 2012-05-04 and 2012-05-05 captures (ts 20120503104742, 20120504013138, 20120504184847, 20120505100132) publish Sunday Pre-Open 16:15 and weekday Pre-Open 16:45; the 2012-06-16 capture (ts 20120616193925) and every later capture through 2015-04-06 (ts 20140401181938, 20150406000146) publish Sunday Pre-Open 16:00 and weekday 16:45. That brackets the Sunday-queue move 16:15 -> 16:00 to 2012-05-05..2012-06-16 with NO CME notice stating the day. This is the same platform-wide, undated Sunday-queue move already documented in energy_metals.rs (bracketed there to 2012-05-28..2012-06-07 from the metals/energy hours pages), so weather almost certainly moved on the same unannounced day — but LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES forbids encoding it. Recommended handling, mirroring energy_metals.rs: carry the narrowest sourced queue (Sunday 16:15-17:00, Mon-Thu 16:45-17:00) across the dated history without asserting a cutover, and put the wider current queue (Sunday 16:00-17:00) only on the fixed-current / knowledge-bound row.

NO PRIMARY CAPTURE OF THE FUTURES GRID BETWEEN 2022-06-30 AND 2025-03-10. The continuous chain of CME specification captures runs 2010-02-06, 2010-07-25, 2012-05-11, 2013-09-10, 2015-09-04, 2016-12-01, 2018-06-01, 2019-11-18, 2021-04-22, 2021-07-28, 2022-06-30 — all reading "Sunday 5:00 p.m. - Friday 3:15 p.m. / Daily trading halts 3:15 p.m. - 5:00 p.m." After 2022-06-30 CME's product pages became fully client-rendered, so no archived capture resolves the interval. It is closed only by SER-9519's own "Current CME Globex Hours" column on 2025-03-10, which is a primary CME statement of the state immediately before the cutover. I did not exhaustively read every CME SER / Globex / market-data notice across 2022-07..2025-03; no source I retrieved shows any different weather grid in that window.

WEATHER OPTIONS WERE A FLOOR (OPEN-OUTCRY) PRODUCT FOR MOST OF THE IN-SCOPE HISTORY, AND THE DAY THEY MOVED TO GLOBEX IS NOT SOURCED. This is the one place where the family genuinely split by instrument type, and an implementer keying options to this profile needs to know. Evidence retrieved: (a) CME's weather trading-hours page, 2011-09-27 raw HTML, puts each product on two lines (futures then options) and fills Open Outcry only on the options line and the Electronic columns only on the futures line — e.g. Canadian Monthly Weather Cooling: Open Outcry cell = '
08:30-15:15', Electronic (Weekday) cell = '17:00-15:15
 ' (https://web.archive.org/web/20110927011404id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading_hours/weather-hours.html). (b) CME's US Monthly Weather HDD OPTIONS specification, capture 2012-08-20 and 2014-08-27: "Trading Hours / (All times listed are Central Time) / Open Outcry / (Trading Floor) / MON-FRI: 8:30 a.m.-3:15 p.m." (https://web.archive.org/web/20140827025018id_/http://www.cmegroup.com/trading/weather/temperature/us-monthly-weather-heating_contractSpecs_options.html); the options quote/time-and-sales tabs on that page are '_quotes_openOutcry_options.html' while the futures tabs are '_quotes_globex.html'. The same "MON-FRI: 8:30 a.m.-3:15 p.m." persists on captures at 2016-05-02, 2019-07-22, 2021-02-25, 2021-07-28 and 2022-06-30, with the option product record still carrying pitEligible=1 as late as the 2022-06-30 capture. (c) SER-7606R, 14 March 2016, states it flatly: "The weather futures contracts will continue to be listed for trading on the CME Globex electronic trading platform, and the weather options contracts will continue to be listed for trading on the CME trading floor." (https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7606R.pdf). (d) A 2007 CME press release corroborates the original design: "The futures contracts will trade only on the CME Globex(R) electronic trading platform from 5 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. Chicago time the following day. ... Options on all CME weather futures will be traded on CME's trading floor from 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. Chicago time." (https://investor.cmegroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/cme-launch-weekly-weather-futures-and-options-contracts). (e) By the 2024-05-18 capture the option product record reads pitEligible=0, and today every weather option publishes the Globex grid (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/weather/hdd/chicago-hdd-monthly/specs/options). BRACKET: after 2022-06-30 and by 2024-05-18. Adjacent but NOT dispositive: CME Globex Notices of 2023-05-15 and 2023-07-31/2023-08-21 list NEW weather futures/options for Boston, Burbank, Houston, Philadelphia, Paris and Essen on Globex effective Sunday 2023-05-21 (trade date 2023-05-22) and Sunday 2023-08-27 (trade date 2023-08-28) — those are product launches for cities that had no such contract before, not a venue migration of the pre-existing options. NO primary document I retrieved states the day the legacy weather options moved off the trading floor onto Globex, so no cutover may be encoded for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MODEL: if this key is meant to answer for weather OPTIONS as well as futures, then across roughly 2010-01..2022-06 the options' executable window was a same-day floor session 08:30-15:15 CT (a `regular`/RTH session, ssm 30600-54900, MON-FRI) and NOT the Globex wrap. If the key is documented as covering the Globex-listed weather complex (which is what every current product page shows for both futures and options), then regular stays empty throughout and the options' floor era is simply out of the key's scope — but that scope decision must be written down, not left implicit.

The exact composition of the ~179 roots was not enumerated from a single CME machine-readable slate; the root list above is assembled from CME's own fact card and product-slate PDFs plus the current product pages. CME's product-slate PDFs predate the current Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 quarterly seasonal strips, which appear only on the live product pages.
reuse_verdict:
NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. Suggested: MarketHoursKey::GlobexWeather => "globex_weather", backed by a new schedules/futures/us/weather.rs.

The trap here is exactly the one the brief warns about: weather's CURRENT envelope is byte-identical to the existing GlobexEnergy (energy_metals) profile — extended SUN+MON_THU 17:00->16:00, order_entry SUN 16:00-17:00 plus MON_THU 16:45-17:00, regular empty, daily and weekend close true. Matching the current row is NOT a reason to reuse, and here it would be actively wrong:

1. HISTORY DIVERGES FOR FIFTEEN OF THE SIXTEEN IN-SCOPE YEARS. Weather closed at 15:15 CT from the January-2010 floor until 2025-04-13. Over that same span GlobexEnergy closed at 16:15 CT (2010 floor) and then 16:00 CT from Monday 2015-09-21. So for 2010-01 .. 2025-04-13 — about 92% of the audited timeline — reusing GlobexEnergy would report weather's daily close 60 to 75 minutes late every single day, and would fabricate a 2015 cutover weather never had. The 2015-09-04 and 2016-12-01 captures of CME's weather specification both still read 3:15 p.m., which is direct primary evidence that weather sat out the NYMEX/COMEX 2015 move. The two grids only converged on 2025-04-13, and by coincidence of arithmetic, not by a shared notice: SER-9519 names only weather.

2. PRODUCT-FAMILY SEMANTICS ARE DISJOINT. GlobexEnergy is documented as NYMEX CL/NG/HO/RB/BZ/PL/PA plus COMEX GC/SI/HG — physically-settled energy and metals on two different DCMs. Weather is CME (XCME), financially settled off a published temperature index, with its own Globex security group (HW futures / W7 options), its own rulebook chapters (CME 403/403A, 405/405A), its own Daily Bulletin section (24), and its own hours-notice channel. CME has never announced a weather hours change inside an energy/metals notice or vice versa; SER-9519 addresses "all weather futures and options" and nothing else. Folding weather into globex_energy would also mean a future CME notice touching only one of the two families could not be encoded without splitting the key anyway — a breaking persisted-wire change, since key names are the serde wire format.

3. NO OTHER EXISTING KEY IS CLOSE. globex_equity_index, globex_grains, globex_fx, globex_interest_rates, globex_livestock and globex_cryptocurrency all publish different grids; livestock is a same-day RTH family with an empty extended, the polar opposite shape.

Implementation shape, following the energy_metals.rs precedent (regular: &[], the wrap-around Globex session in extended, the Pre-Open in order_entry):
 - AT_2010_FLOOR: extended = [{SUN_PLUS_MON_THU, open 61200, close 54900}], regular = &[], order_entry = the narrowest sourced queue only (see the Pre-Open note in `unsourced`); has_daily_close true, has_weekend_close true.
 - Revision keyed 2025-04-13 (local opening day; CME's stamped Effective Date is 2025-04-14 — record both in the module comment): extended = [{SUN_PLUS_MON_THU, open 61200, close 57600}].
 - CURRENT / fixed table: same extended, order_entry = [{SUN_ONLY, 57600, 61200}, {MON_THU, 60300, 61200}].
 - Module doc must state that CME ClearPort is deliberately not modelled, and must state whether the key covers weather options (see the options/floor entry in `unsourced` — that decision has to be explicit).
